signal.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare.
signal.summary: On November 10, 2026, Google Cloud announced a U.S. preview of Gemini for healthcare, an enterprise system that combines specialized healthcare skills, clinical record connectors, controlled agents and audit trails. Read integrations for Epic and Oracle Health are listed among partner capabilities. The product is aimed at providers and payers, not at replacing clinical judgment or becoming a general consumer diagnosis service.

signal.title: Gemini Decisions API: Fast, calibrated multimodal decisions
signal.summary: Google introduced the Gemini Decisions API on November 11, 2026, powered by Gemini Decision 1, for probabilistic classification rather than general text generation. The announcement lists up to 1,000 questions per request, 256,000-token multimodal inputs and a $0.10 per million-input-token list price, with no output-token billing. SXF explains the difference between advertised model-compute speed and end-to-end latency and shows how to design human-review thresholds instead of treating a confidence score as proof.

signal.title: Google Search gets a major upgrade with Gemini 4 Hydrogen
signal.summary: Google announced the global integration of Gemini 4 Hydrogen into Search on November 12, 2026, aiming to interpret complex, multi-part queries and present more visual, structured results with links to relevant sources. A separate model launch establishes Hydrogen's developer positioning and published pricing. signal.title: GPT‑6 Cyber: Advancing the frontier of aligned cybersecurity agents

Initial access is limited to approved Daybreak Red customers, so this is not a general ChatGPT model release.

signal.title: Measuring how AI agents handle everyday wet-lab science
signal.summary: OpenAI introduced BioBasicsBench on November 6, 2026 with biotech partner Ligo, using 100 routine wet-lab tasks built from raw scientific evidence. At the highest compared reasoning setting GPT-6 Astra earned 66.7% mean rubric credit versus 43.8% for GPT-5.6 Sol. These are partial-credit benchmark averages, not percentages of experiments safely completed without scientific oversight.
